data.title: Russell 3000 reconstitution adds Red Robin, Vera Bradley and removes SES AI, Thryv
data.description:
FTSE Russell has released a preliminary list of companies set to join or leave the Russell 3000 Index as part of its 2026 annual reconstitution.

Among consumer discretionary companies slated to join the index are Paramount Skydance (SKYD), Red Robin Gourmet Burgers (RRGB), NN (NNBR), Vera Bradley (VRA) and Newegg Commerce (NEGG).

Meanwhile, consumer discretionary companies set to leave the index include SES AI Corporation (SES), Thryv Holdings (THRY), Wheels Up Experience (UP), Lee Enterprises (LEE) and Rent the Runway (RENT).

The newly reconstituted indexes are scheduled to take effect after the U.S. market close on December 11.

data.title: Chegg, SES AI, and others are set to leave Russell Microcap Index
data.description:
FTSE Russell has released a preliminary list of companies set to leave the Russell Microcap Index as part of its 2026 annual reconstitution.

Among consumer discretionary companies slated for removal are Chegg (CHGG), SES AI (SES), Surf Air Mobility (SRFM), Interface (TILE), and Lindblad Expeditions (LIND).

No consumer discretionary companies are currently slated to join the index.

The newly reconstituted indexes are scheduled to take effect after the U.S. market close on December 11.

data.title: ConocoPhillips to sell Norway, Teesside assets to Vår Energi for $3.9B
data.description:
ConocoPhillips (COP) has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Norway business and its 40.25% interest in and operatorship of the U.K. Teesside oil terminal to Vår Energi for total consideration of $4.425B, less agreed upon adjustments of approximately $0.5B as of the Jan. 1, 2026, effective date.

The transaction is expected to close by the end of the first quarter 2027 subject to approval by the Norwegian Ministry of Energy and regulatory conditions, the Houston-based oil and gas producer said.

At closing, Vår Energi will assume the post-effective date balance sheets of the properties. Total consideration is expected to be $3.9B, including the remaining 2026 tax liability of ~$1.4B, payable in the first half of 2027, and net cash proceeds of approximately $2.5B, the company said.

Proceeds will be earmarked for general purposes and for discretionary share repurchases in 2027 to supplement the company’s long-standing commitment of returning ~45% of cash from operations to shareholders.

The transaction includes the entire issued share capital of ConocoPhillips Skandinavia AS and ConocoPhillips (U.K.) Teesside Operator Limited, which together hold the company's Norway and Teesside assets and associated decommissioning liabilities.

The Norway business includes ConocoPhillips' (COP) interests in producing assets on the Norwegian continental shelf, anchored by the operated Greater Ekofisk Area in the North Sea, as well as interests in eight partner-operated fields across the Norwegian Sea and northern North Sea. It also includes the company's interest in the Norpipe oil pipeline and certain non-operated infrastructure. The Teesside business includes the Teesside oil terminal and related pipeline infrastructure.

In 2025, the Norway business produced approximately 120 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day. Year-end 2025 proved reserves associated with the sale properties were approximately 221 million barrels of oil equivalent.

data.title: Trump hosts meme coin dinner as token drops
data.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump, who has earned hundreds of millions of dollars from his $TRUMP meme coin, said at a dinner for the token’s top holders on Sunday that his support for the cryptocurrency was driven by a desire to strengthen the United States’ economic competitiveness.

“I’m doing it for the United States ... If we don’t do it, China’s going to do it,” Trump told attendees at his golf club outside Washington, according to reports. It was the third time Trump had held a gala for the top owners of his meme coin, which once soared as high as $75 ​but has fallen to a record low of under $1.

The gala’s access and perks are divided by tiers for the 185 holders of $TRUMP, the president’s meme coin. The top 29 investors are invited to a VIP reception, and the top four will receive a “TRUMP 18K Gold Watch”, according to the event’s website.

Attendees qualified for the dinner based on their time-weighted holdings of the $TRUMP ⁠coin from September 30 to November 16. Reports say organizers indicated that 185 crypto wallets met the criteria for Sunday's dinner, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just ​130 wallets when the contest concluded on November 16.

The President reported earning more than $1B from his cryptocurrency ventures in 2025, according to his financial disclosures filed with the U.S. Office of Government Ethics and reported in mid-2026.

The May 2025 event's biggest $TRUMP holder was China-born crypto billionaire Justin Sun, who had $18.5M of the token. This time, there was no Sun at the event signing ​autographs, as per Reuters.

Bitcoin ETFs: (IBIT), (ARKB), (GBTC), (BRRR), (BTCO), (HODL), (BTCW), (FBTC), (BITB), and (EZBC).

data.title: Brookfield agrees to buy PGP Glass from Blackstone for $1.7B
data.description:
• Brookfield (BN) has agreed to acquire PGP Glass, a global specialty glass packaging manufacturer, from funds managed by Blackstone (BX) Private Equity through its flagship private equity strategy for $1.7B, the companies  said on Monday.
  • PGP manufactures specialty glass packaging for cosmetics and perfumery, specialty food and beverage, and pharmaceutical industries, serving leading global brands in more than 70 countries.
  • The company offers end-to-end solutions comprising design, mold-making, specialty glass manufacturing, and decoration, supported by three manufacturing facilities across India and Sri Lanka, alongside an extensive global logistics and warehousing network.
  • Brookfield’s investment will be funded through the Brookfield Capital Partners strategy and its affiliate Brookfield Business Corporation. The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory and government approvals. Closing is expected in Q1 2027.

data.title: China's gold imports said to have surged to record $209B through Oct.
data.description:
• China’s gold imports reportedly surged to a record $209B so far this year, in an unprecedented buying spree that followed a promise by top officials to make their country into the world’s marketplace instead of just its factory.
  • The shift began in January — the same month Vice Premier He Lifeng made that vow in front of a crowd at Davos — as the value and volume of bullion imports more than doubled from the month before.
  • Non-monetary gold purchases continued climbing in the 10 months through October, reaching a historical high that’s equivalent to nearly 8% of overall imports in the period, the latest data showed Friday, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: MSCI reportedly discussed avoiding Indonesia downgrade with Prabowo, Dalio
data.description:
• MSCI Inc. (MSCI) CEO Henry Fernandez conveyed a willingness to consider alternatives to a two-step downgrade of Indonesia’s stock-market status in recent direct talks with President Prabowo Subianto, Bloomberg reported.
  • Fernandez and Prabowo spoke for more than an hour on a Nov. 10 conference call brokered by Ray Dalio, the billionaire founder of hedge fund Bridgewater Associates, the report said.
  • Dalio, who has acted as an informal adviser to Prabowo’s government, joined the call, as did Rosan Roeslani, the CEO of the Indonesian sovereign wealth fund Danantara. A few other minders and close aides were also dialed in, the report added.
  • Indonesia faces scrutiny from MSCI after the global index provider ​warned the country's stocks could be removed from its indexes in 2027 ‌and ⁠the market relegated two steps down from an emerging market to "standalone" status, bypassing the frontier rating.
  • Fernandez said during ​the call ⁠that MSCI did not necessarily intend to downgrade Indonesia and instead would continue to advise Indonesian officials on the ⁠steps ​they would need to take to ​ensure they meet the necessary standards, according to the report.

data.title: Monday's Economic Calendar
data.description:

The Chicago Fed National Activity Index, or CFNAI, is a monthly index that tracks overall economic activity and inflationary pressures.

The flash Composite Purchasing Managers' Index, or PMI, provides an early estimate of current private sector output by combining information obtained from surveys of around 1,000 manufacturing and service sector companies.

data.title: Trump calls for Nvidia to rehire Jensen Huang amid China probe
data.description:
• President Donald Trump late on Monday said bringing Jensen Huang back to Nvidia (NVDA) would be the best move for both the company and the United States.
  • “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang,” he said in Truth Social post.
  • The comments come as U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that the U.S. is seeking answers from Nvidia (NVDA) on its chip sales to China and ​will find out who was in charge of compliance at the ‌company formerly led by Jensen Huang, who resigned following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
  • "We've been in touch with the ​temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do ​need answers. ... It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because ⁠we want to know what the culture was," Bessent told the CBS ​program "Face the Nation."
  • Once the most valuable company, Nvidia is now fourth behind Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT) and Alphabet (GOOG). The chipmaker's shares fell 14% on Friday and are down ~34% this year.

data.title: Asian markets extend losses after Wall Street selloff; U.S. futures rebound
data.description:
Asian equity markets traded mostly lower on Monday, extending last week's global technology-led selloff as concerns over AI valuations continued to weigh on investor sentiment. South Korea's Kospi bore the brunt of the selling, falling more than 5%, even as U.S. equity futures rebounded following Wall Street's steep weekly losses. Japan's markets remained closed for a public holiday.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng (HSI) declined 0.64%, China’s Shanghai Composite (SHCOMP) slipped 0.96%, Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 edged down 0.20%, while India’s Sensex (SENSEX) lost 0.47%.

China’s state-backed funds invested a record 90B yuan ($13.5B) in ETFs on Friday, stepping up efforts to support the country’s stock market as a prolonged selloff pushed the benchmark CSI 300 Index into bear-market territory.

Australia's composite PMI falls to the lowest level in over five years.

Spot gold rebounded around 1.7% to $3,584 an ounce, recovering after a sharp 8.9% decline last week. Brent crude slipped 0.30% to $92.29 a barrel, while WTI fell 0.18% to $83.26, extending last week's losses. 

Wall Street tumbled on Friday, pushing the S&P 500 into correction territory, with the index down 3.7% and the Nasdaq falling 5.3%. However, U.S. futures rebounded in Asian trading on Monday, with S&P 500 futures up 2.05%, Nasdaq 100 futures gaining 2.88%, and Dow futures up 1.44%.
